title: How Much Does a Squarespace Website Cost in 2026? Plans, Fees and Design Costs
excerpt: Squarespace raised its prices in July 2026. Here's what a Squarespace website costs now, from the plan and add-ons to hiring a designer, with my own prices.
seoTitle: How Much Does a Squarespace Website Cost? (2026 Prices)
seoDescription: Squarespace raised its prices in July 2026. Plans now cost $19 to $99 a month. Here's what a site really costs in year one, on your own or with a designer.
imageAlt: A Squarespace website I designed for a mediation practice, shown on a laptop
body:
Published February 18, 2026 · Updated November 25, 2026 with Squarespace's new prices

Squarespace raised its prices in July 2026, so a lot of the numbers you'll find online are out of date. I build Squarespace websites for a living, so I went through Squarespace's own pricing pages and added up what a website actually costs now, from the plan itself to the extras people don't expect. I also included what it costs to have someone design it for you, with my own prices.

The short answer

A Squarespace plan costs $19 to $99 a month if you pay for the year up front, or $25 to $139 if you pay month to month. Most small businesses I work with use the Core plan, which is $29 a month, or $348 a year.

If you hire a designer, add a one-time design cost on top of that. My Website-in-a-Day is $1,500 and my custom websites start at $3,000. Big agencies usually charge $10,000 or more.

All prices are in US dollars and come from squarespace.com and acuityscheduling.com, checked on November 25, 2026. Prices before tax.

Squarespace plans and prices in 2026

Every plan includes hosting, a free SSL certificate, mobile-friendly templates and 24/7 support. Every plan also lets you sell. The differences are mostly in the fees you pay when you sell and in the extra store and marketing tools.

PlanPaid yearlyPaid monthlyCost per yearOnline store feeCard rate
Basic$19/mo$25/mo$2282%2.9% + 30¢
Core$29/mo$39/mo$3480%2.9% + 30¢
Plus$49/mo$65/mo$5880%2.7% + 30¢
Advanced$99/mo$139/mo$1,1880%2.5% + 30¢

"Cost per year" is the yearly price. If you pay monthly instead, Basic works out to $300 a year and Core to $468. Card rates are for Squarespace Payments with standard cards. American Express and some business cards are 3.2% + 30¢ on every plan. You can see the full list on Squarespace's pricing page.

What changed in July 2026

Squarespace raised its prices in July 2026 by up to 26%, depending on the plan. On yearly billing, Basic went from $16 to $19 a month and Core went from $23 to $29 a month (PetaPixel covered it here). If you signed up before then, you'll see the new price when your plan renews.

Which plan do you need?

  • Basic ($19/mo): Fine for a portfolio or a simple site where you aren't selling much. It only allows 2 contributors, and Squarespace takes an extra 2% of anything you sell through your online store.

  • Core ($29/mo): This is the one I recommend to most of my clients. There's no 2% store fee, you get unlimited contributors, and it comes with a free year of business email through Google Workspace.

  • Plus ($49/mo): Worth it if you run a growing online store. Card fees drop to 2.7% + 30¢, and the fee on courses and memberships drops from 5% to 1%.

  • Advanced ($99/mo): For high-volume shops and course creators. It has the lowest card rate and no fee at all on courses and memberships.

A quick way to decide between Basic and Core: Core costs $120 more a year than Basic. The 2% store fee on Basic costs you $120 once you sell about $6,000 a year through your website. If you expect to sell more than that, Core is the cheaper plan.

Other costs to budget for

The plan price isn't the whole bill. Here's what else usually comes up.

Your domain name

If you pay for a plan yearly, Squarespace gives you a free domain for the first year. After that it renews at the regular price, which is $22 a year for a .com on Squarespace Domains. If you already own a domain somewhere else, you can connect it to your site instead.

Business email

Core, Plus and Advanced include a free year of Google Workspace, so you can have an email like you@yourbusiness.com. After the first year, Google Workspace is billed per person, per month.

Card processing fees

Whenever someone pays you by card, the payment processor takes a cut. With Squarespace Payments it's 2.9% + 30¢ on Basic and Core, and less on the higher plans. Stripe and PayPal charge their own rates. I break all of these down, including the 2% Basic store fee, in my post on the hidden costs of Squarespace.

Online booking (Acuity Scheduling)

If clients book appointments with you, you'll probably want Acuity Scheduling, which Squarespace owns. It's a separate subscription:

Acuity planPaid yearlyPaid monthlyGood for
Starter$16/mo$20/moOne person with one calendar
Standard$27/mo$34/moText reminders, packages and up to 6 calendars
Premium$55/mo$69/moHIPAA (for therapists and health practices) and up to 36 calendars

If you're a therapist or work in healthcare and need a signed HIPAA agreement, that's only on Premium. Prices are on Acuity's pricing page.

Email newsletters

Collecting email signups on your site is free. Sending newsletters from Squarespace takes an Email Campaigns plan, which starts at $8 a month (paid yearly) for up to 500 emails a month and goes up to $118 a month for 500,000. You can also connect Mailchimp on the Core plan and up.

Courses and memberships

If you sell courses or memberships through Squarespace, there's a fee on each sale: 7% on Basic, 5% on Core, 1% on Plus and 0% on Advanced.

Templates

Squarespace templates are free on every plan. You only pay extra if you buy a third-party template or plugin, which most sites don't need.

What a Squarespace website costs for the first year

Here are three common setups, using yearly billing. These are just the Squarespace costs. Design costs are in the next section.

SetupWhat's includedFirst year
Simple websiteBasic plan, free domain for the first year$228
Service businessCore plan + Acuity Starter$540
Therapy practiceCore plan + Acuity Premium (HIPAA)$1,008

Add card fees if you take payments online. From the second year on, add $22 a year for a .com domain.

What it costs to have a Squarespace website designed

This is the part most people are really asking about. There are three main ways to get your site built, and the costs are very different.

1. Doing it yourself

Design cost: $0, plus your time.

Squarespace makes it look easy, and if you have a good eye for design, you can make a template work. But a lot of my clients come to me after spending weeks on their own site. Things don't line up the way they want, the phone version looks off, and they've spent whole weekends searching for how to fix it.

A DIY site usually takes 40 to 80 hours. If your time is worth $100 an hour, that's $4,000 to $8,000 of your time, and it's easy to miss SEO settings you didn't know existed.

2. Hiring a freelance Squarespace designer

Design cost: about $1,500 to $5,000, depending on the size of the site.

This is where I work. You talk to the person building your site directly, and a site usually takes days or weeks instead of months. A good freelancer will also set up your SEO, connect your booking or payment tools and show you how to make edits yourself.

3. Hiring a big agency

Design cost: $10,000 to $25,000 or more.

Agencies give you a whole team, like a copywriter, a designer and a developer, and their work is often beautiful. I've seen quotes my clients got from agencies before they came to me, and they're a lot for a small business. Agency projects also tend to take 3 to 4 months.

How to choose a Squarespace designer

Whoever you hire, here's what I'd check before you sign anything:

  • Sites like yours. Ask to see a few sites they've built for businesses similar to yours.

  • Reviews from real clients. Squarespace's own Marketplace and 99designs both show reviews from people who hired the designer through them.

  • A clear price. Get the number of pages, rounds of changes and the total in writing before you start.

  • SEO setup. Ask what's included, so your site can show up on Google from day one.

  • Training. You should be able to update your own site once it's done.

  • Squarespace Circle status. Circle partners can get you a discount on your Squarespace plan.

As for me, I've built more than 350 websites over the past 7+ years, and I'm a Squarespace Circle Platinum Partner. I have 115 reviews on my Squarespace Marketplace profile (listed as Clementine Studio) and a 5.0 rating from 100+ reviews on 99designs. You can see some of my work in my portfolio.

A few reviews from the Squarespace Marketplace

"Mali was fantastic. I'm very happy with the website and she made the process so easy."

"I had a great experience working with Clementine Studio on my website updates. She listened carefully to what I needed and suggested an approach that worked even better than my original idea."

My prices

I used to not list my prices, which I know is frustrating when you're trying to budget. So here they are.

ServicePriceWhat you get
Website-in-a-Day$1,5001 to 5 pages on Squarespace, built in one day with your logo and colors. Changes until the end of the day and a training call. You'll need your text and photos ready.
Custom WebsiteFrom $3,0005+ pages on Squarespace, Shopify or WordPress, in about 3 to 4 weeks. 3 rounds of revisions, SEO setup and a training call.
Hourly Help$150/hrUpdates, layout changes and troubleshooting on a site you already have.
Monthly MaintenanceAbout $300/moSend me questions or changes anytime, and I'll fix things if something goes wrong.

Your Squarespace plan is separate from my design fee. As a Circle Platinum Partner, I can get you 25% off a new yearly Squarespace plan, which brings Core from $348 down to $261 for the year. You can see everything I offer on my services page.

How to spend less on Squarespace

  • Pay for the year up front. Squarespace says yearly billing saves up to 36%, and it comes with the free domain.

  • Pick your plan based on how much you'll sell. If you'll sell more than about $6,000 a year through your site, Core costs less than Basic.

  • Add things when you need them. You can start on Core and add Acuity or Email Campaigns later, as your business grows.

  • Use the free trial. Every site starts with a 14-day free trial, and you don't need a credit card for it.

Is Squarespace worth the price?

For most small businesses, I think so. Hosting, security and support are included, so you aren't paying separately for hosting and plugins or keeping them updated. Your booking and newsletters can also live in the same place as your website.

It isn't the cheapest option if all you need is one page and you're comfortable building it yourself. But it's the platform I build most of my clients' sites on, because they can update it on their own once it's done.

Frequently asked questions

Is Squarespace free?

No. Squarespace doesn't have a free plan, but every site starts with a 14-day free trial, and you don't need a credit card to start one. You'll need a paid plan to publish your site.

How much is Squarespace per month?

Squarespace costs $19, $29, $49 or $99 a month when you pay for the year up front, or $25, $39, $65 or $139 a month when you pay monthly.

How much does a Squarespace website cost per year?

The plan alone is $228 to $1,188 a year on yearly billing. Most small businesses pay about $348 a year for the Core plan, plus any add-ons like Acuity Scheduling.

Does Squarespace include hosting and a domain?

Hosting is included on every plan. A domain is free for the first year when you pay yearly. After that, a .com renews at $22 a year.

How much does it cost to hire a Squarespace designer?

Freelance Squarespace designers usually charge about $1,500 to $5,000 for a full website, and agencies charge $10,000 or more. My Website-in-a-Day is $1,500, and my custom websites start at $3,000.

How do I find a good Squarespace designer?

Start with Squarespace's own Marketplace, where you can compare designers' portfolios, starting prices and client reviews. Then ask a few of them for examples of sites like yours and a written price before you decide.

Did Squarespace raise its prices?

Yes. In July 2026, Squarespace raised prices by up to 26%. On yearly billing, Basic went from $16 to $19 a month and Core went from $23 to $29.

Can I cancel or change my Squarespace plan?

Yes. You can change or cancel your plan anytime, and the change takes effect at the end of the period you've already paid for.

Want help figuring out your costs?

If you're not sure which plan or add-ons you need, I'm happy to help. Book a free 20-minute consultation and I'll tell you what your website would cost, both on Squarespace and with me.

You can’t import:

There’s a reason so many of us are craving real connection online - especially in spaces where we can learn, grow, or feel supported in some kind of transformation.

Whether you're building a workout program, a virtual classroom, or a coaching container, Squarespace + Member Areas makes it surprisingly simple to create a space where your community can gather, stay accountable, and keep showing up.

I’ve seen this work especially well for:

  • Online schools or creative courses

  • A 6-week curriculum that unlocks weekly

  • Pre-recorded breathwork or meditation sessions

  • Monthly templates or design tools for creative businesses

title: Does Squarespace Have An SEO Plugin Similar to Yoast in 2023?
excerpt: Yes it does! Using this plugin, Squarespace users can now run scans on each page of their website to give them more insight into what areas to improve to optimize their chances of being favored by Google.
seoDescription: Yes. SEOSpace is an SEO plugin for Squarespace, similar to Yoast. It scans each page of your site and shows you what to improve for Google.
body:
Yoast is a popular plugin that helps WordPress users improve their websites for Search Engine Optimization (SEO). Squarespace users have been long overdue for a similar plugin in the same vein! In April 2023, Henry Purchase, founder of Rough Water Media, released their long-awaited plugin: SEOSpace.

Using this plugin, Squarespace users can now run scans on each page of their website to give them more insight into what areas to improve to optimize their chances of being favored by Google.

I’ve been following Henry Purchase for a few months before the plugin was released. He’s well-versed in both Squarespace and SEO, and has released multiple YouTube helpful videos on his channel on the topic of optimizing for SEO. I’ve found his videos are super informational, and he seems to be very passionate about helping Squarespace users get the most out of the platform without breaking the bank.

I purchased a “DIY Plan” ($9.99/mo) and tested my own website to see how it works. I downloaded the Chrome plugin, put in my targeted keyword “squarespace experts,” and ran a Premium Scan on my homepage. After the scan was complete, it gave me a score: 49/100.

The plugin caught a few issues that were likely holding my page up from being ranked, such as having multiple H1 tags and missing image alt text. I had forgotten that I created a section on the homepage that was only visible on mobile, which included an H1 tag and an image. Nice catch, SEOSpace!

The plugin also used my keyword “squarespace experts,” and caught any instances where it should be placed on my website in order to improve my chances of ranking for it (a Premium Scan perk).

I fixed the outstanding errors, ran the Premium Scan again, and got up to an 89/100. There was one fix that I had missed - my meta description didn’t have enough characters. Once I fixed it, I was tempted to run the scan again just to feel the satisfaction of seeing a perfect score. But I decided against it, since I wanted to save them, as my plan comes with 10 Premium Scans.

I plan to go through each page on my website with my intended keyword to optimize my entire site. I’m still working on my SEO strategy, though, so I feel like that should come first.

Overall Thoughts

I think the emergence of SEOSpace is an awesome start to helping Squarespace users optimize their site for SEO. Their “Free Plan” includes 10 Basic Scans per month, which looks for baseline refinements such as checking broken links, image sizes, meta tags, and other baseline refinements to get your website up to speed. It’s a good place to start if you just want to test the plugin out.

It’s a great quick way to check every page of a Squarespace website for optimization suggestions, and it’s the first of its kind.

If you upgrade to their “DIY Plan,” you’ll be able to enter a keyword and location to get suggestions on where to place them throughout your page.

Henry and his team at SEOSpace are very responsive and open to suggestions as they continue to make improvements and iron out kinks since their first launch date. With the “DIY Plan,” you get access to the SEOSpace community, where you can offer suggestions, get help, and connect with other SEOSpace users.

I plan to upgrade to the highest tier “Agency Plan” to see how the “Discover search keywords” function works once I have my SEO strategy in place. With this plan, it looks like there’s some additional features that are on their way as well, such as automated monitoring, scans, and reports. I’ll report back when I do.

If you’d rather not do your SEO yourself, I can set it up for you. See my SEO services.

title: Should You Update Squarespace To The Latest Version?
excerpt: Currently, there’s no way to migrate content from 7.0 to 7.1 without starting from scratch and rebuilding. Is it worth the trouble? Read along to find out.
seoDescription: There's no way to move a Squarespace 7.0 site to 7.1 without rebuilding it. Here's when upgrading is worth it, and when you may want to stay on 7.0.
body:
Currently, there’s no way to migrate content from 7.0 to 7.1 without starting from scratch and rebuilding. Is it worth the trouble? Read along to find out.

There’s no doubt that websites built on the new Squarespace 7.1 version are faster, cleaner, and more versatile than websites built on the old Squarespace 7.0 version.

But if your website has any of the following, it may be worth reconsidering whether migrating from version 7.0 to 7.1 is the best choice for you:

  1. You’ve been grandfathered into a low annual or monthly subscription.
    At the time of writing this, a Business Plan is $23/mo if paid annually, and $33/mo if paid monthly. Some clients I’ve worked with in the past created their Squarespace website many years back, when the subscriptions were as low as $15/mo. If you migrate from 7.0 to 7.1, you’ll be starting a new website, which means you’ll have to say goodbye to your cheaper plan. Make sure you check how much you’re paying now, and compare it to Squarespace’s current pricing before you do the switchover.

  2. You’re happy with your existing site.
    Squarespace version 7.1 offers new features such as the Fluid Engine (a grid-like drag-and-drop content editing experience) and site-wide animations. But if you’re happy with your website now, and don’t need to add any bells and whistles, you’re good to stay on 7.0. As of now, Squarespace still offers support for both versions, so there’s really no added benefit in switching over.

  3. You have lots of complex pages… or a lot of pages in general.
    It’s relatively easy to migrate text to a new 7.1 site — if you like copying and pasting. But if you have lots of complex pages on your website (ex. long pages with multiple images, galleries, videos, etc), it just might not be worth the hassle. If you still insist on switching over and don’t want to do it yourself, you can contact me for an hourly quote to handle the migration.

  4. You have a Member Area with lots of members.
    It’s not an easy process to migrate members from one version to the next. If you’re using Squarespace’s Member Areas, make sure you know what you’re getting yourself into. You can learn more on Squarespace’s support page.

Overall, if you’re looking for speed, a cleaner look, and SEO improvement, then migrating to 7.1 may be the direction you want to go. However, if you’re happy with your 7.0 website and don’t need to add any new features that 7.1 offers, there may not be a compelling reason to upgrade.

If you decide to switch to 7.1, I can build the new site for you. See how my website builds work.
summary: Currently, there’s no way to migrate content from 7.0 to 7.1 without starting from scratch and rebuilding. Is it worth the trouble? Read along to find out.
